messages:
priya: quick sync — enterprise customer (Acme Inc) wants per-route quotas + per-team billing attribution. asking for timeline: include in v1 launch or push to v1.1?
emma: can we scope v1 to per-tenant + per-route limits and meter exports with route_id tags, defer per-team cost allocation to v1.1?
mike: FYI metering impact: we need route_id + optional team_id in events. current pipeline only emits org_id + model_id + tokens. adding fields touches ingestion, storage schema, and invoice generation.
chris-b: edge cases to call out: 1) model fallback (requested model vs executed model) — billing should reflect executed model. 2) cache/KV hits — if KV satisfied, do we charge tokens? 3) streaming partial failures where tokens are double-counted on retry.
leah: agreed on fallback = executed model. for KV hit we should bill 0 tokens for generation but still log a cache_hit metric for attribution. need legal check on free credits vs cache hits.
sam: acceptance criteria proposal (short):
- API supports per-route quota config (soft cap, hard cap, grace window)
- Metering events include route_id and team_id (optional)
- Billing exports map executed_model -> price_per_token used at invoice time
- UI shows quota usage per-route and per-tenant; team allocation view is v1.1
- Rollout: canary on 5% orgs + rollback flag
priya: add edge acceptance: retries must be de-duplicated in metering, and cache hits must not increment billable tokens. document fallback billing rule.
emma: UX notes: limits UI needs clear copy for soft cap vs hard cap. soft cap should show throttling behavior (warn -> degrade) and hard cap should block requests with 429 + billing unaffected.
mike: backend tasks rough list: 
- ingest schema change: add route_id/team_id tags
- invoice pipeline: apply executed_model rates (migration window for historical charges)
- metering dedupe: idempotency via request_id token
- quota enforcement: per-route limiter with bursting policy
chris-b: technical edgecases: 
- per-second vs per-month quotas (windowing) — need sliding window or token-bucket semantics
- cross-region requests: route defined by API route, but enforcement must be global for tenant
- rate-sculpting for L7 proxies: must support downstream headers for client identification
leah: question: who owns migration plan for historical invoices if we change price granularity? finance needs a runbook.
priya: finance + billing should own invoice migration; product to write migration requirements. add acceptance criteria: migration runbook approved.
sam: small API sketch: 
`POST /v1/quotas` body: { "route_id": "string", "tenant_id": "string", "soft_cap": {"tokens": 10000, "window": "1m"}, "hard_cap": {"tokens": 20000, "window": "1m"}, "grace_seconds": 30 }
emma: can we use same UI components as entitlement pages? reuse reduces design effort.
deploy-bot: staging quota-enforcement-2 deployed to staging — tests: quota enforcement, metering events with route_id present.
mike: dev checklist for v1: schema migration run in feature-flag mode, billing export includes route_id but team_id optional, UI shows per-route usage, canary rollout hooks in console.
chris-b: outstanding tradeoffs: do we support per-team in v1 behind a flag? doing so increases backend complexity (team mapping for API keys). leaning to postpone.
priya: decision: ship v1 with per-tenant + per-route quotas, metering with route_id, executed_model billing. per-team allocation behind feature flag for v1.1. action items: product PRD draft by EOD Friday, engineering impact doc by Monday, finance migration runbook draft by next Wed.
emma: will add acceptance criteria and copydeck to PRD.
leah: I'll loop in finance and legal for credits and cache billing semantics.
sam: I'll prototype dedupe logic and sliding-window limiter in a small upstream PR.
priya: thanks all — tagging followups: @emma (PRD), @mike (ingest/schema), @leah (finance/legal), @sam (prototype). :thumbsup:
